rows.statement: The kernel reads resume_offset= as the swap header's position inside the resume= partition, counted in PAGE_SIZE units and needed only for a swap file; this host boots with resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=3795013 because its only swap area is a file.

source.quote: at which the swap header is located, in <PAGE_SIZE> units (needed only for swap files)

rows.statement: On btrfs the resume offset comes from btrfs inspect-internal map-swapfile, whose -r form prints the value already divided by the page size; on this host it prints 3795013, equal to the cmdline resume_offset, so the configured offset points at the current swap header.

source.quote: that will print the device physical offset and the adjusted value for

rows.statement: filefrag is the wrong tool on btrfs: its physical_offset column is a btrfs logical address, not the device offset; on this host filefrag reports the first extent at block 3530821 while map-swapfile reports 3795013, so a resume_offset copied from filefrag would point at the wrong place.

source.quote: The value is the physical offset on the device.

rows.statement: A btrfs swap file must be NODATACOW, which also means no data checksums and no compression for that file; lsattr on /swap/swapfile shows the C attribute, so the file meets the requirement on this host.

source.quote: swapfile - must be NODATACOW (i.e. also NODATASUM, no compression)

rows.statement: Hibernation can only write to an active swap file; /proc/swaps lists /swap/swapfile as an active file swap of 31722876 KiB, so the precondition holds at capture time and fails if the file is swapped off.

source.quote: the swap file has to be active (ie. be present in /proc/swaps) so that it can be used for suspending.

rows.statement: Deleting and recreating the swap file can move its header, so resume_offset must be re-derived whenever the file is recreated; the file's birth time 1791060333 (2026-10-03 17:45:33 -03) is the recheck trigger: a different birth time means re-run map-swapfile before trusting hibernation.

source.quote: the location of its header need not be the same as before.

rows.statement: systemd-hibernate-resume hands the resume device to the kernel by writing its major:minor to /sys/power/resume; on this host /sys/power/resume reads 253:0, which is /dev/mapper/root (stat hex fd:0), so the device the kernel will resume from this boot is the swap file's filesystem device.

source.quote: Internally, it works by writing the major:minor of selected device node to

rows.statement: /sys/power/resume_offset overrides the cmdline offset, so the value that matters at hibernation time is the sysfs one; here it reads 3795013, equal to both the cmdline and map-swapfile, so no writer has changed it since boot.

source.quote: Using this sysfs file will override any values that were set using the kernel command line for disk offset.

rows.statement: The mkinitcpio resume install hook adds systemd-hibernate-resume to the image when systemd is at least version 255; this host runs systemd 262 and the booted UKI's initramfs carries usr/lib/systemd/systemd-hibernate-resume, so this busybox-hook image's resume hook hands off to that binary when it runs; which writer set /sys/power/resume this boot is not shown.

image_size is an upper limit in bytes on the hibernation image, and the image must fit in free swap; here image_size is 12835467264 bytes against about 20 GB of free swap at capture, so the headroom check passes but shrinks as swap use grows.

source.quote: string representing a non-negative integer that will be used as an upper limit of the image size, in bytes.
